name: Chicago
lede: The Canyons, the Oaks, and a deep bench of park gems — Chicago's disc golf lives in the suburbs and it is seriously good. We're publishing the metro's best first.
introParagraphs: Chicago's disc golf scene is a suburban circuit with a superstar: The Canyons at Dellwood Park in Lockport, a 27-hole championship layout with variant holes, water hazards, and an on-site pro shop that draws players from across the Midwest. The Oaks in Mokena offers another 27-hole marathon through giant oaks, free and friendly.

Katherine Legge in Hinsdale is the gentle park-style course with a dog park attached, and Highland Park in Joliet rounds out the top tier with wooded-and-open variety. All four of our published Chicago courses are free.
New here? Start at Katherine Legge, then work your way up to The Canyons — it's a full day.

faqs.question: How many disc golf courses are in the Chicago metro?
faqs.answer: Around 65 courses across the metro and its suburbs. We're publishing the best first — 4 are live today, with more added every week.

faqs.question: What's the best disc golf course in Chicago?
faqs.answer: The Canyons at Dellwood Park — a 27-hole championship layout with variant holes, water hazards, and an on-site pro shop. It's the highest-rated course in the metro by a wide margin.

faqs.question: Are Chicago's disc golf courses free?
faqs.answer: Yes — all four of our published courses (The Canyons, The Oaks, Katherine Legge, Highland Park) are free to play.

faqs.question: What's the best beginner course in Chicago?
faqs.answer: Katherine Legge in Hinsdale — a short, friendly park course that also doubles as a dog park. The Oaks is another approachable option with its 27 gentle holes.
